First, a privilege is defined as a thing that is conferred upon a person by others; we don’t speak of a dog’s "superhuman hearing privilege" or a bird’s "flight privileges" because we all understand that these things are innate in the animal.

And yet, similar natural characteristics in humans are often referred to as "privileges" despite the fact that they can in no way be considered such by any normal understanding of the word; no conscious entity "grants" a human a healthy body or a stable neurochemistry. Therefore these things can only be advantages, not "privileges."

And that brings us to the second issue, which is that the word “privilege” implies an advantage which is undeserved and unearned, and thus something for which the "privileged" individual supposedly owes a debt or obligation to someone else (to one's country, or "society").

Basically, replacing semantically-neutral words like “characteristic” with the semantically-loaded word “privilege” is an overt attempt at emotional manipulation, to make the fortunate feel guilty for natural characteristics over which they had no more control than their eye color or height.

It's a semantic switcheroo designed to manipulate people into viewing themselves as "naturally" deserving to be put down because of their supposed "privileges." If our human characteristics are suddenly unearned “privileges” magnanimously granted to us by a beneficent "society" then the "authorities" in said society (the current flavour of the month being the "oppressed victim-ocracy") arguably have the power to demean and diminish those who are so "privileged."

But when we recognize that self-ownership and personal agency are the birthrights of every single human being, abrogation of those rights is seen for what it truly is: Violation. Usurpation. Theft.

For example, using the phrase "white privilege" pardons the government for its systematic violations of the rights of minorities, as if the way white people are preferentially treated in Western societies is somehow a "privilege," an “extra” thing conferred upon some but not others.

They pull the old semantic switcheroo, and the onus of the guilt seems to fall upon those who are fortunate enough to have received this (undeserved) gift.

But if we recognize the truth, that such treatment is the birthright of everyone, then the onus falls where it belongs: on those authoritarian actors who act independently or collectively to rob minorities of what is rightfully theirs by virtue of their humanity.

Being harassed relatively less by cops is not a "privilege." Being treated more leniently by the courts is a not "privilege" conferred upon white people who otherwise would be treated as poorly as minorities.

And being seen as thinner and more attractive simply by virtue of one's own thinness and attractiveness is not, and never was, a Privilege.

To refer to decent, respectful treatment, or the admiration for one's hard work, or one's natural endowments and biological characteristics, as a "privilege" is to imply that nobody actually deserves it.

And historically speaking, to implicate privilege in such a way, my friends, is textbook early-stage fascism.
